Policy Name: Cigna ACDF (CMM-601: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion)
Referred Sections: Malposition or Failure of Implant/Instrumentation or Structural Bone Graft

Medical necessity indications.Guideline Category: Malposition or Failure of Implant/Instrumentation or Structural Bone Graft
Required findings: Post‑operative imaging demonstrates malposition or failure of the implant/instrumentation or structural bone graft (e.g., migration, screw breakage or loosening, rod breakage/bending, loss of curve correction, decompensation, etc.)
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-601.6 > Malposition or Failure of Implant/Instrumentation or Structural Bone Graft

Required findings: ≥ 6 months elapsed since the prior ACDF at the same level
Daily neck pain of clinically significant intensity causing functional impairment (e.g., inability to perform household chores, prolonged standing)
Physical examination findings concordant with the reported pain

Failure to achieve clinically meaningful improvement after BOTH of the following (unless contraindicated):
  • Prescription‑strength analgesics, steroids, gabapentinoids, and/or NSAIDs for ≥ 6 weeks
  • Provider‑directed exercise program for ≥ 6 weeks
Post‑operative imaging performed ≥ 6 months after the prior fusion shows pseudoarthrosis at the requested level(s)
Post‑operative MRI/CT findings concordant with symptoms
No unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorder (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid or alcohol use disorder)
Documentation of nicotine‑free status (never‑smoker or abstinent ≥ 6 weeks with objective cotinine testing)
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-601.6 > Unremitting Neck Pain with Pseudoarthrosis

Required findings: ≥ 6 months elapsed since the prior ACDF at the same level

Both of the following symptoms:
  • Significant daily pain causing functional impairment
  • Unremitting radicular pain to the shoulder girdle and/or upper extremity resulting in disability

Physical exam demonstrating any of: dermatomal sensory deficit, motor weakness (biceps/triceps), reflex changes, shoulder abduction relief sign, or positive nerve‑root tension sign (e.g., Spurling’s maneuver); OR unremitting radicular pain without concordant objective findings

Failure to achieve clinically meaningful improvement after at least TWO of the following (unless contraindicated):
  • Prescription‑strength analgesics, steroids, gabapentinoids, and/or NSAIDs for ≥ 6 weeks
  • Provider‑directed exercise program for ≥ 6 weeks
  • Epidural steroid injection(s) or selective nerve‑root block(s) at the same level(s)
Post‑operative imaging ≥ 6 months after prior fusion shows pseudoarthrosis at the requested level(s)

Post‑operative MRI/CT demonstrates neural structure compression at the requested level(s) concordant with symptoms and exam, caused by herniated disc, synovial/arachnoid cyst, central/lateral/foraminal stenosis, or osteophytes
No unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorder
Documentation of nicotine‑free status (never‑smoker or abstinent ≥ 6 weeks with objective cotinine testing)
≥ 6 months elapsed since the prior ACDF at the same level

Any of the following symptoms:
  • Upper or lower extremity weakness, numbness, or pain
  • Fine motor dysfunction (e.g., difficulty buttoning, handwriting, hand clumsiness)
  • Gait disturbance
  • New‑onset bowel or bladder dysfunction
  • Frequent falls

Physical exam demonstrating any of: grip‑and‑release test abnormality, ataxic gait, hyperreflexia, Hoffmann sign, Babinski sign, tandem walking ataxia, inverted brachial radial reflex, increased muscle tone/spasticity, clonus, myelopathic hand
Post‑operative imaging ≥ 6 months after prior fusion shows pseudoarthrosis at the requested level(s)
Post‑operative MRI/CT shows findings concordant with symptoms and exam caused by cervical spinal cord compression or cervical spinal stenosis
No unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorder
Documentation of nicotine‑free status (never‑smoker or abstinent ≥ 6 weeks with objective cotinine testing)

Non-Indications: Repeat ACDF performed for pain or radiculopathy without documented pseudoarthrosis or implant failure
Procedures performed less than six months after the initial ACDF at the same level
Cases lacking required conservative therapy trial, imaging, nicotine‑free verification, or with unmanaged significant mental/behavioral health disorders
Important criteria & exceptions: Patient must be nicotine‑free: either a never‑smoker or abstinent ≥ 6 weeks with objective cotinine testing (serum, urine, or saliva) within normal range
Unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid or alcohol use disorder) preclude medical necessity
Conservative management must be documented for the specified duration (≥ 6 weeks of medication and/or physical therapy; ≥ 6 weeks of at least two modalities for radiculopathy)
Imaging must be performed no earlier than six months after the prior fusion to assess pseudoarthrosis
Documentation required: Operative report of the prior ACDF
Current post‑operative imaging (X‑ray, CT, or MRI) demonstrating pseudoarthrosis or implant failure
MRI/CT report showing neural element compression (for radiculopathy) or cord compression/stenosis (for myelopathy)
Detailed physical examination findings documenting neurologic deficits or concordant pain
Records of conservative therapy: medication prescriptions (type, dose, duration) and physical therapy or other exercise program notes for ≥ 6 weeks
Epidural steroid injection or selective nerve‑root block reports (if used for radiculopathy)
Objective nicotine‑free verification (cotinine test result) or statement of never‑smoker status
Psychosocial assessment confirming absence of unmanaged significant mental/behavioral health disorders
